`final class FrameBufferPool`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.render.framebuffer` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [FrameBufferPool.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/render/framebuffer/FrameBufferPool.java)

Lends offscreen framebuffers by owner and nesting depth, grows them when a draw does not fit, and frees the ones left unused.

## Description

The effects, the shader passes and [`DrawRaster`](/reference/drawing/drawraster/) borrow their framebuffers here, so that a size that changes on every frame does not create one each time.
A framebuffer grows to the next power of two of the size asked, and is freed after 5 seconds without use.
Each draw of a UI bridge calls `releaseUnused()`, so a host that draws through the UI bridge has nothing to call.

## Method details

<a id="FrameBufferPool-method-allocate"></a>

### allocate

`IFrameBuffer[] allocate(Object owner, int depth, int count, int width, int height)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns `count` framebuffers of at least `width` × `height` pixels for `owner` at nesting depth `depth`, the same ones as last time when they are large enough.
Use one depth per level of nesting, so that a draw inside a draw gets its own framebuffers.

### releaseUnused

`void releaseUnused()` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>
